reasoning_traces.think:
EnbPI addresses the core challenge of time-series conformal prediction by relaxing exchangeability assumptions and eliminating data waste from calibration splits. It achieves this through an ensemble of base learners, each producing out-of-sample residuals. These residuals are aggregated into a sliding window to estimate prediction intervals. This design allows full utilization of data while adapting to regime shifts. In GSI, this maps to Bayesian inference where posterior uncertainty is derived from ensemble residuals rather than fixed priors. For GSE, the sliding window enables dynamic adjustment of prediction intervals based on recent performance, crucial for weekly forecasting. The method's strength lies in its ability to maintain validity even under change points, provided the window size is adequate. Failure modes include overfitting due to too small a window or poor model stability. The key insight is that conformal prediction can be made practical for time series by combining ensemble learning with adaptive windowing.
